site_place: West and South West London — London Boroughs of Kensington and Chelsea, Hammersmith and Fulham, and Wandsworth (Richmond upon Thames also listed as an area of operation)
site_venue: Rotating Emergency Winter Night Shelters hosted across seven church/community venues (one venue per night of the week, three circuits); year-round casework delivered from four partnering day centres; central services hub at Argon House, Argon Mews, Fulham, London SW6 1BJ. Individual shelter/day-centre venue names are not published on the website.
site_activity: Emergency overnight winter shelter accommodation and year-round homelessness casework, advice and advocacy
last_delivery_what: Ran the 2024-25 Emergency Winter Night Shelter season (November–April) plus year-round casework; 569 people found a safe place to sleep in the night shelters and 423 guests moved into housing
local_trigger: Rising homelessness in London, with rough sleeping at near-record levels; a growing cohort of newly recognised refugees made homeless after eviction from Home Office accommodation, plus increasing numbers of under-35s experiencing homelessness (Glass Door Annual Impact Report 2025-26)

programmes.name: Casework / Advice and Support Service
programmes.what: Year-round advice and support from trained caseworkers based at four partnering day centres across West and South West London; helps guests secure housing, a bank account and ID, access benefits and healthcare, resolve insecure immigration status and get referrals to specialist services

programmes.name: Emergency Winter Night Shelters
programmes.what: Three rotating night-shelter circuits each winter (November–April) serving approximately 105 guests per night (35 in each circuit) across seven venues in Kensington & Chelsea, Hammersmith & Fulham and Wandsworth, one venue for each night of the week

programmes.name: Women's Shelter and Women's Casework Drop-in
programmes.what: Gender-informed provision for women experiencing homelessness — a dedicated Women's Night Shelter (run for a third year running) plus a weekly 1-to-1 Women's Casework Drop-in

programmes.name: Mailbox Service
programmes.what: Postal address / mailbox service for guests, run from the Glass Door services hub at Argon House, Fulham

_certifications_note: APPLICANT-SUPPLIED CERTIFICATIONS (not from public materials): the four boolean administrative self-certifications below are what a real applicant attests on the intake form and are not published anywhere. They are set true here because all four are established registered charities delivering services to vulnerable people, for whom a safeguarding policy, public liability insurance, own-name banking and a conflict-free application are universal and, for safeguarding, legally expected. No specific unknowable detail (e.g. a named Designated Safeguarding Lead) is invented — those stay blank.
